_comment: #1641 fleet OOM kill order for oci-apps (24G RAM, ~326G of declared cgroup ceilings, zram 12G + 24G disk swap). The ONE declaration per service is build.json runtime.oom_score_adj, applied by _shared/oom-priority.nix; this file is the ordering and the reasoning, and _shared/test-oom-priority.mjs fails if a service listed under `applied` disagrees with its build.json. Lower = killed LAST. The kernel kills the highest oom_score first. Host-side tiers already in force (cloudy-t-infra protection/system-packages.json): connectivity sshd/wg -900, protection -800, docker daemon +500; containers are NOT inherited from the daemon (docker sets 0), so the values below are what the container tasks really carry. -1000 is deliberately not used: it exempts a task from the cgroup OOM killer too, so a runaway would wedge against memory.max instead of being reaped.

tiers.why: c3-infra MCP: the fleet's own remote hands. Restart policy is 'no' (owner policy), so a kill means it stays down and the owner loses every MCP tool.
Everything that declares nothing: app/data/obs containers, kg-store, mail, vault, caddy, edge. The kernel's own memory-size badness ranks these.
Restartable on demand, cosmetic or re-creatable state.
Chromium farm: biggest memory per unit of value.
JVM scanner, on demand only: killed before anything else in this list.

deferred._why: Not changed in #1641 because recreating the container kills live work (a runner mid-build or an agent mid-session, and Ship can itself run on the oci-apps runner). Each is a one-line runtime.oom_score_adj in its build.json to be applied during a quiet window.

infra-bld_gha-runner.note: Largest declared memory footprint on the VM (64G of ceilings): the prime hog candidate under a Gradle/Nix build.

user-ai_cloudy-ai-claude-api.note: Agent runner; the load-shedder already treats it as sheddable demand.
